# select_user_role (Resource)

One role granted directly to a user, identified by email address, on the whole organization or on one resource. Use one of these per grant.

## About

Each `select_user_role` grants one role directly to one user, on one scope. Grants that Terraform does not manage are not changed.

Omit `scope` to grant the role on the whole organization. To grant it on one resource, set `scope.type` and `scope.id`.

This resource is backed by SELECT's v2 API, at `/v2/users/{email}/roles`.

### Users who have not signed in yet

SELECT keeps a role grant against an email address. The user does not have to exist in SELECT yet: if they have not signed in, the grant takes effect when they first sign in through your identity provider. This is why the provider has no user resource. Users come from your identity provider, and you identify them by email address.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# The user does not have to have signed in yet. The grant takes effect when
# they first sign in through your identity provider.
resource "select_user_role" "alice_admin" {
  email = "alice@example.com"
  role  = "admin"
}

# One role on one Snowflake account.
resource "select_user_role" "bob_account_editor" {
  email = "bob@example.com"
  role  = "editor"
  scope = {
    type = "snowflake_account"
    id   = "2c3f5d9e-8a1b-4c6d-9e0f-1a2b3c4d5e6f"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `email` (String) The email address of the user to grant the role to. The user does not have to have signed in yet: the grant takes effect when they first sign in. Changing it forces a new grant.
- `role` (String) The role to grant: `admin`, `editor`, `monitor_editor`, `viewer` or `team_creator`. Changes in place.

### Optional

- `scope` (Attributes) The resource the role applies to. Omit it to grant the role on the whole organization. `id` is required for every `type` except `organization`. Changing it forces a new grant. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--scope))

### Read-Only

- `create_time` (String) When the role was granted — RFC 3339 UTC, e.g. 2026-06-05T10:30:00Z.
- `etag` (String) Opaque strong ETag for this grant. Sent as `If-Match` on updates and deletes so a change made outside Terraform cannot be silently overwritten.
- `id` (String) The grant's identifier in SELECT, assigned when the role is granted. Use it with `terraform import`, as `email/id`, to bring an existing grant under management.
- `update_time` (String) When the grant was last updated — RFC 3339 UTC.

<a id="nestedatt--scope"></a>
### Nested Schema for `scope`

Required:

- `type` (String) The kind of resource the grant applies to: `organization`, `snowflake_organization`, `snowflake_account`, `databricks_account`, `databricks_connection`, `bigquery_connection`, `aws_account`, `tableau_site` or `usage_group`.

Optional:

- `id` (String) The resource's identifier: the Snowflake organization name, the Snowflake account UUID, the Databricks account id, or the id SELECT gave the Databricks connection, BigQuery connection, AWS account, Tableau site (its LUID) or usage group. Leave it unset for `organization`.

## Import

`select_user_role` can be imported using the email address and the grant ID, separated by a forward slash:

```bash
terraform import select_user_role.example alice@example.com/<role_id>
```

The provider splits the address at the last forward slash, so an email address that holds a forward slash also works.

To find the grant ID, list the user's roles with the API. Only direct grants can be imported: `is_default` must be `false` and `granted_from_team_name` must be `null`.

```bash
curl -s https://api.select.dev/v2/users/alice@example.com/roles \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SELECT_API_KEY" \
  -H "x-tenant-id: $SELECT_ORGANIZATION_ID" | jq '.items[] | {id, role, entity, is_default, granted_from_team_name}'
```

## Additional Information

### Only direct grants

A user can hold a role in three ways: granted to them directly, inherited from a team they belong to, or held by everyone in the organization by default. This resource manages only direct grants. Manage a team's roles with `select_team_role`, and the default roles with `select_default_role`. If the provider reads a grant that is not direct, it treats the grant as gone.

### Only `role` changes in place

A change to `role` is an update. A change to `email` or `scope` revokes the grant and makes a new one.

### A grant that already exists

If SELECT refuses the grant with a conflict, the same role can already be granted to the user on the same scope. Import that grant instead of creating it again.

### Changes made outside Terraform

Every write carries the grant's `etag` as an `If-Match` header, so an update or delete is refused if the grant changed since Terraform last read it. When that happens, run `terraform apply -refresh-only` to pick up the current state and then apply again.
